Clones ship fast.

When software is easy to copy, I look for advantages growing stronger as the business grows.

1. Data flywheels
Users generate useful data to help you improve the product.

2. Network effects
The product becomes more useful as more people use it.

3. Hard-to-enter markets
Regulated fields such as health care and fintech take more time and effort to enter.

A small profitable software business doesn't need to win a venture-scale race. At 1,000 customers paying $50 a month, revenue is $50,000 a month. This is meaningful for many indie founders, even if a competitor copies parts of the product.

What makes a startup defensible?
Is a small software company profitable?
What are network effects?

#startups #saas #bootstrapping #entrepreneurship #indiehackers

VC expectations sound unreal.

At a TechCrunch investor panel, I heard investors say going from $0 to $10M in annual recurring revenue no longer excites them. They were talking about companies racing toward $100M quickly.

As a bootstrap founder, I see $10M ARR as an enormous business. A profitable company is possible without following a venture capital growth plan.

I also heard investors discuss large companies still trying to maintain product-market fit. A big revenue number doesn't mean the work is finished.

Do startups need venture capital?
What does $10M ARR mean for a founder?

Comment INTERVIEW for the prompts 👇

Practice interviews with tougher questions.

Use ChatGPT as a mock hiring manager before your next interview. Ask it to challenge vague answers and score each response.

1. Start with a mock interview
Act as a tough hiring manager interviewing me for [ROLE] at [COMPANY]. Ask 1 realistic question at a time. Challenge vague answers with follow-ups. Score my answer from 1 to 10 and tell me how to improve.

2. Add context
Upload your resume and paste the job description if available.

3. Make it harder
Now use my resume and job description to ask me harder questions.

Practice out loud. Keep the specific examples from your work and rewrite weak answers in your own words.

Comment CODES for more study commands 👇

Stop asking AI for answers.

Use these 10 commands to study, recall, and explain a topic. Put your topic after the command and add your notes if available.

1. ELI5
Explain the topic in plain words.

2. 80/20
Start with the most useful 20% of the topic.

3. MAKE-STICKY-NOTES
Turn the key facts into a sticky note guide.

4. FEYNMAN-TECHNIQUE
Explain it simply until gaps stand out.

5. MAKE-MINDMAP
Map the main ideas and their connections.

6. QUIZME
Ask 1 question at a time.

7. MAKE-VISUAL-STUDYGUIDE
Create a 1-page study sheet.

8. FIRSTPRINCIPLES
Break the topic into its base ideas.

9. SOCRATES
Teach through questions instead of a quick answer.

10. MAKE-SCHEMATIC
Draw a schematic of the parts and how they fit.

Choose 1 command, add a topic, and keep asking questions until you explain it yourself.

ChatGPT explanations shouldn't need decoding.

When an answer feels too dense, I add ELI Cactus to my question. It means ‘explain like I'm a cactus.’ It's a playful twist on ELI10, or ‘explain like I'm 10.’

Try: ‘Explain [topic]. ELI Cactus.’ If ChatGPT misses the cue, ask: ‘Explain [topic] in simple words. Give me the first step.’

I use it to find an easy place to start. Ask again about any part you don't understand. Check key facts before you rely on them.

AI skills? Show what you've built.

If you're applying for jobs, give employers a relevant AI project to look at. Tie the project to the role you want.

You don't need to buy a course to start brainstorming. Open ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini. Replace the blank with your target role and paste this:

"""
I'm applying to this role _____.

Brainstorm 10 easy AI project ideas I can do for <$100 that are highly relevant to the role and would help my resume stand out because everyone's obsessed with AI.
"""

The prompt asks for 10 ideas within a budget. Pick one tied to the work you'd do in the job.

Ask the AI to walk you through the project, including which tools you'd need and what to do first. Check the costs before starting.

Then do the work. Add the finished project to your resume and explain what you built. A list of ideas isn't a completed project.

Your AI agrees. You're still stuck.

If every AI chat ends with praise for your next idea, ask for a reason to rethink it before you start another project.

Comment “POSITIVE” and I’ll send you everything 👇

Stop letting AI flatter you.

Try a 5-minute exercise about real moments from your day. Use ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini with this full prompt:

I am rewiring my brain through positive psychology. Guide me through a 5-minute daily exercise to train my attention to notice good things in my life.

Ask me 1 question at a time.

1. Help me identify 3 specific things that went well today, even tiny moments
2. For each one, ask why it happened and why it mattered to me.
3. Help me choose my favorite moment, close my eyes, and mentally relive it for 20 seconds, remembering what I saw, heard, and felt
4. Ask me what I appreciate most about it

Don't give me generic compliments, force positivity, or dismiss difficult emotions.

Finish by helping me notice 1 small good thing tomorrow.

Automation comes last, not first.

Asking AI for an answer is stage 1. The work gets more useful when you use AI to test ideas, learn your process, and handle bigger jobs with clear rules.

The 5 stages:
1. Ask AI: Get an answer.
2. Think with AI: Find gaps in your ideas.
3. Teach AI: Show it how you like work done.
4. Delegate to AI: Give it a meaningful assignment.
5. Automate with AI: Have it repeat the work on a schedule.

At stage 2, ask AI to find blind spots and question whether the work needs to exist.

At stage 3, give AI context, examples, rules, and feedback. Let it ask questions. Check the output, then save your process as a reusable skill.

At stage 4, give AI a real job with several files. Check every figure and piece of evidence before you trust the result.

At stage 5, schedule a reliable skill. Start with drafts for human review. Add tools or connectors when the job needs fresh data.

Get the full 5-stage guide here:
